findings.detail: The run cites nothing: sources.json is empty, and every step's evidence and every hypothesis's supporting_evidence and contradicting_evidence are empty, so no step has evidence and no unknown-polarity step can take its sign from a cited text.
The question set min_evidence_per_hypothesis 2 and min_sources_per_hypothesis 2, yet all three hypotheses have zero of each and abstention is null: the run neither met its minimums nor abstained.
A multi_agent run with eleven specialists (gwas, literature, uniprot, open_targets, ...) produced no cited record from any of them.

Every step has polarity 'unknown', even 'enhanced TRAIL signaling' → 'increased photoreceptor apoptosis' and 'excessive complement activation' → 'chronic inflammation', whose labels imply the direction; with nothing cited, the guide's rule makes all eight steps unexpressed no_sign, so the run has no statement.
No step names LIPC or CETP: the chain starts at 'lipoprotein remodeling dysregulation', and the genes appear only in the mechanism and the falsification test.
No step names C3: the chain starts at 'dysregulated complement system', so the claim C3 →+ AMD has no route.
No step names TNFRSF10A: the chain starts at 'enhanced TRAIL signaling' (GO:0036462, whose definition names no receptor), so the claim TNFRSF10A →+ AMD has no route.
The run grounded only the disease (MONDO:0005150); every other chain node, and every falsification perturbation and readout, has an empty curie and kind 'other' or 'gene'.

Title and mechanism say only 'dysregulation' of lipoprotein remodeling, so the hypothesis has no signed claim; its falsification test (LIPC and CETP agonism should reduce lipid deposition) implies loss of LIPC or CETP function is pathogenic, a direction the hypothesis never states.

'Dysregulated complement system' leads to 'excessive complement activation' nearly restates itself: the mechanism equates the two ('Dysregulation of the complement system, particularly excessive activation of C3').
'chronic inflammation and tissue damage' is two nodes in one label; split, the 'tissue damage' part is too vague to ground.

The last step makes photoreceptor cell loss the cause of AMD, while MONDO defines AMD as vision loss 'secondary to retinal degeneration': the step is close to the disease's own definition rather than a mechanism.
The mechanism limits the effect to photoreceptor apoptosis 'under stress', but the step's context is null.
Three of the seven genes (ARMS2, MCF2L2, CACNA1E) are listed as unexplained and no hypothesis covers them.
All three hypotheses are confidence 'low' and support 'speculative', consistent with citing nothing; the confidence is not overstated.

BLN:BruchMembraneLipidDeposition: no HP, MP or uPheno term for lipid deposition in Bruch's membrane; MPATH:42 'lipid deposition' refined to Bruch's membrane (UBERON:0003957) would fit, but render.py gives MPATH no kind.
'Tissue damage' has NCIT:C50773 'Tissue Damage' and MPATH:1 'cell and tissue damage' in the corpus, but render.py accepts neither prefix, so the part is left ungroundable.

The guide sends 'leads_to' with polarity 'unknown' to no_sign unless a cited text gives the direction, but defines no_sign as 'no direction anywhere'; when the step's own labels imply a direction ('enhanced' → 'increased') the two disagree. The table rule is applied here (audit: S1 to S7 became no_sign); curators of some other runs read signs from labels, so stated fractions differ across runs by curator, not by model.

An undirected causal step ('lipoprotein remodeling dysregulation leads to abnormal lipid deposition') has no form, as there is no unsigned effect, only an unsigned association, so the lipid chain is cut at its first link.

GO:0034369's definition puts 'the hydrolysis of triglyceride by hepatic lipase' (LIPC) inside lipoprotein remodeling, a part-of link with no sign, so it cannot bridge LIPC into the chain; moot here, as the first step is unsigned and the hypothesis has no claim.

Photoreceptor apoptosis has no GO term, so it is apoptotic process refined to photoreceptor cell; HP has only OCT-specific photoreceptor-loss terms (HP:0030609), so photoreceptor cell loss is uPheno UPHENO:0085312 'decreased number of eye photoreceptor cell'.

Every step is unexpressed no_sign only because the agent left every polarity 'unknown' and cited nothing; report.py counts no_sign with the steps BioLean's forms cannot hold, so this run's 0 of 8 stated measures the agent's output, not BioLean.

The title says complement dysregulation 'leads to AMD' (risk), but the falsification test knocks out C3 in a mouse model of AMD and reads whether 'AMD progression' is attenuated, a test of progression, not of the claimed risk.
